papers.title: Multiplex Single-Cell Bioprinting for Engineering of Heterogeneous Tissue Constructs with Subcellular Spatial Resolution.
papers.abstract: Tissue development, function, and disease are largely driven by the spatial organization of individual cells and their cell-cell interactions. Precision engineered tissues with single-cell spatial resolution, therefore, have tremendous potential for next generation disease models, drug discovery, and regenerative therapeutics. Despite significant advancements in biofabrication approaches to improve feature resolution, strategies to fabricate tissues with the exact same organization of individual cells in their native cellular microenvironment have remained virtually non-existent to date. Here we report a method to spatially pattern single cells with up to eight cell phenotypes and subcellular spatial precision. As proof-of-concept we first demonstrate the ability to systematically assess the influence of cellular microenvironments on cell behavior by controllably altering the spatial arrangement of cell types in bioprinted precision cell-cell interaction arrays. We then demonstrate, for the first time, the ability to produce high-fidelity replicas of a patient's annotated cancer biopsy with subcellular resolution. The ability to replicate native cellular microenvironments marks a significant advancement for precision biofabricated in-vitro models, where heterogenous tissues can be engineered with single-cell spatial precision to advance our understanding of complex biological systems in a controlled and systematic manner.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文未涉及任何AI或机器学习方法，仅专注于多路单细胞生物打印技术。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not integrate AI/ML into bioprinting workflow, no computational model, no autonomous decision-making or experimental validation of an AI method.

summary_zh.motivation: 以单细胞空间分辨率构建异质组织模型需高精度生物打印。
summary_zh.method: 利用多通道单细胞打印技术，以亚细胞精度排列多达八种细胞表型。
summary_zh.result: 实现了患者癌症活检组织的高保真复制，并系统评估细胞微环境对行为的影响。
summary_zh.validation: 通过细胞相互作用阵列和活检复制验证打印精度与生物学功能。

summary_en.motivation: Precision-engineered tissues with single-cell resolution require advanced biofabrication to replicate native cellular microenvironments.
summary_en.method: A multiplex single-cell bioprinting method is reported that can spatially pattern up to eight cell phenotypes with subcellular precision.
summary_en.result: High-fidelity replicas of a patient's annotated cancer biopsy were produced, enabling systematic study of cellular microenvironment effects on behavior.
summary_en.validation: Validation was performed via precision cell-cell interaction arrays and by reproducing the spatial organization of a real biopsy sample.
